page.layout: Two engraved medallion portraits side by side at the top, each with its legend around the rim (left: LYCVRGVS and LACEDÆ.; right: DIRCEVS). Below them, one column of running text in two paragraphs, the first on Lycurgus and the second on Dircaeus, with no margin notes. A small woodcut ornament sits at the foot of the page, below the text. Running head at top, page number at top left.

main_text.l: LYCVRGVS
LACEDÆ.
DIRCEVS
LYCVRGVS apud Lacedæmonas leges fanxit, impe-
rante Latinis Aremulo, circiter annum mundi 3090. ante
Chriftum natum 872. alij referunt ad annū mundi 3181. ante
Chriftum natum 781. Primùm omnium 28. feniores inftituit,
qui Regibus affisterent, & populari principatui repugnarent,
rurfúfque populi iuribus aduerfus tyrannidem faueret. Secun-
dò agros æqualiter diuifit. nummum aureum & argenteum ex
vfu fuftulit: ferreum folum vtendum imperauit: priuatum lu-
xum inhibuit. Cætera qui cupit noffe, adeat Plutarchum in vi-
ta Lycurgi. Fuit oratione breuis: quas tradidit leges, finxit fe ex
Apollinis Delphici oraculo tenere, ne reiicerentur, quòd fe-
uerae effent: indotatas iubebat accipi vxores, vt prolis non ar-
genti gratia nuberent viri: tum vt ne puellae pauperes, innuptae
relinquerentur. non inuentione legum magis quàm exemplo
clarior extitit: fiquidem nihil lege vlla in alios fanxit, cuius nõ
ipse primus in se documenta daret. Iustinus multis in locis. Au-
guft.de Ciui.Dei.lib.2.cap.16.& lib.10.cap.13. Plutar.in vita Ly-
curgi. Xenophon,in Athenienfium politia.
DIRCEVS, Athenienfis Poëta, deformis quidem, atta-
men tubæ inuentor fuit. Lacedæmonij etenim cùm responsum
accepissent ab Apolline, non alio quàm hoc duce superaturos
se aduersarios Messanos, hunc ducem elegerunt, qui in Cam-
pano agro clangore tubarum Messanos ita exterruit, vt animo
consternati, ac in fugâ versi, facilè victi sint. Vide Mag.Elucida.

page.notes: The two medallion portraits are engravings with legends around the rim; the legends are transcribed above as separate lines. The woodcut ornament at the foot is decorative and not text. No doubtful readings in the body text.
